subject: Post-demo: ACME evaluation — unit-econ deep dive & next tests
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: ACME evaluation — unit-econ deep dive & next tests

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciated the candid product-context you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Recap:
- Primary goal: prove that Redwood can meet ACME’s latency SLO (<=200ms p95) while improving unit economics vs your current hyperscaler endpoint.
- Key constraints: model size (13B family), interactive 1–3 turn UI, ~10M tokens/month expected for initial pilot, compliance needs (SOC 2)
- Competitor touchpoints you called out: hyperscaler managed endpoint (Vertex/Infer) and a third-party inference API.

High-level differentiators we think matter for your evaluation:
- Tailored runtime: continuous batching + KV prefix caching reduces per-token compute for common assistant prompts.
- Cost controls: per-route batching configs, quantization profiles, and explicit cache hit trade-off knobs.
- Observability: token-level cost + latency traces so we can identify where batching hurts p95.

Proposed next tests (brief):
1) Unit-econ microbench (controlled): 500k tokens across three batching configs (batch=1, batch=8, batch=32) to measure per-1M-token cost curve and p95 latency.
2) Cache sensitivity: simulate 0%, 30%, and 60% KV cache hit rates on your top-20 prompts to estimate savings.
3) Cross-provider baseline: run equivalent workloads against ACME’s hyperscaler endpoint (we’ll supply request harness) and Redwood hosted with same model weights/quantization.

Deliverables we’ll provide after tests:
- Per-1M token cost estimate (detailed line items) across scenarios
- Latency and p95 breakouts by batch size and cache hit rate
- A short recommendations doc: suggested config for pilot (canary % / rollout)

Next actions:
- I’ll coordinate with Marissa and Neha to schedule the test window — target to run smoke within 3 business days and full microbench within 7–10 days.
- I attached a quick workbook (redwood_vs_cloud_unit_econ.xlsx) that contains the baseline formulas we’ll use.

If this looks right, can you confirm the token budget for the pilot (you mentioned ~10M/month) and the latency SLO we should assume (confirming <=200ms p95)?

Thanks,
Diego

High-level ballpark per your request — these are estimates with stated assumptions; the attached workbook has the step-by-step calc.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model: 13B dense, quantized to int8 performance profile (our recommended pilot config)
- Average response length: 50 tokens generated per request
- Request overhead: 20 input tokens per request
- Latency SLO target: <=200ms p95 (interactive)
- Batch sizing effects: batch=1 (low latency), batch=8 (balanced), batch=32 (throughput optimized)

Scenario A — No cache, bursty (batch=1): ~1.20 USD per 1M tokens
Scenario B — Moderate batching (batch=8): ~0.78 USD per 1M tokens
Scenario C — High batching (batch=32): ~0.55 USD per 1M tokens
Scenario D — Cache hit 30% (batch=8): ~0.55 USD per 1M tokens (30% fewer generation tokens)
Scenario E — Cache hit 60% (batch=8): ~0.42 USD per 1M tokens

Compared to hyperscaler-managed endpoint (their quote): ~1.10–1.60 USD per 1M tokens depending on their auto-scaling and preemptible mix (they often assume higher baseline because less aggressive KV caching and higher network egress assumptions).

Notes on sensitivity:
- Batching helps compute efficiency but increases tail latency; for interactive UI we expect sweet spot around batch=4–8 for your traffic profile (we’ll validate).
- Cache hit rate multiplies directly into token savings for generation-heavy prompts — even a 30% implementation hit shifts you into a materially lower tier.
- Quantization (int8) reduces GPU throughput cost ~20–30% vs float16 at similar quality; the workbook shows quality delta estimates per prompt set.

Proposed concrete tests we’ll run (I'll own coordination):
- Microbench A: 500k tokens, run batch sizes [1,4,8,16] measuring p50/p95/p99, cost, and maximum achieved qps. (3 business days)
- Cache sim B: replay top-1000 requests from your sample query logs with simulated 0/30/60% key matches; measure token reduction, hit latency, and cost. (2–4 business days)
- Cross-provider run C: run identical harness against your hyperscaler endpoint (we'll provide harness; you just provide endpoint credentials and a test API key) and compare raw cost & p95. (3–5 business days)

I attached SOC2 evidence as requested (soc2-evidence.pdf) and the cost workbook. Also sharing a short sample SLA in the workbook and will pull a separate DOC if procurement wants a formal PDF.

Can Marissa reach out to schedule the test window? We’ll need a contact on your side for the endpoint credentials + a small sample of production queries (anonymized).

Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
